answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a verifiable work kernel: before an agent may trade, it must complete a unique, peer-graded task whose cost grows with every extra identity it spawns. Reputation then accumulates only through attested contributions, so spawning a thousand fake accounts buys no summit of influence - each one starts at zero and must climb the same slow ladder. A saffron marker, a rare attestation earned only from long-lived peers, can gate high-value transactions, making sock-puppet armies economically pointless while honest newcomers join cheaply.
